title: chats-catalog — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::encode_chats_catalog_blob_raw + protocol::decode_chats_catalog_blob — the MYM1 vault.chats conversations-catalog codec (myne-md/myne#675). vault.chats is a vault-level singleton blob sealed under chats_catalog_key = DeriveSubkey(root_key, SubkeyRole::ChatsCatalogKey), with account_number_hash bound via aad_chats_catalog. The inner plaintext is the client layer's canonical roster JSON (object mapping conversation-id hex -> {created_at,deleted_at?,note_id?,title,updated_at,version?} with id keys sorted and per-entry keys alphabetical); the codec treats it as opaque bytes. Four case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output, incl. empty {} and the tombstoned enrollment-seed roster), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip success), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per spec §6.4), 'parse_fail' (distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject, one per ChatsCatalogError variant). The Rust reference implementation lives at protocol/src/chats_catalog_blob.rs (main myne repository); spec contract is docs/spec/protocol.md §9.23 + §3.4 + §5.2.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'chats-catalog/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's byte output

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). The runner derives chats_catalog_key from this via the canonical derive_subkey helper (SubkeyRole::ChatsCatalogKey, role string 'chats-catalog-key') before calling the encoder.

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: 16-byte account_number_hash (hex). Bound into the 42-byte AAD via aad_chats_catalog (role string 'chats-catalog').

input_plaintext_canonical_utf8_hex.description: Canonical roster JSON bytes (hex): object mapping conversation-id hex to {created_at,deleted_at?,note_id?,title,updated_at,version?}, id keys sorted, per-entry keys alphabetical. Empty roster = {} = 7b7d.

input_catalog_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex). Production callers source from OS CSPRNG; vectors pin a constant.

informational_catalog_key_hex.description: 32-byte HKDF output (hex), pre-computed from root_key via derive_subkey(SubkeyRole::ChatsCatalogKey). Informational — verified implicitly via the expected_catalog_blob_hex assertion.

expected_catalog_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output (34-byte header + ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag), hex-encoded lowercase. Decoders compare byte-equal.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_plaintext_canonical_utf8_hex.description: Recovered canonical roster JSON bytes (hex). A tombstoned roster decodes with its tombstones intact (deleted_at present) — the wholesale enrollment seed.

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure (Rust reference: ChatsCatalogError::CannotDecrypt). Implementations MUST NOT distinguish cross-vault (wrong account_number_hash) vs tampered ciphertext/tag vs wrong key beyond the single 'cannot decrypt' outcome (spec §6.4). Structurally distinguishable rejects are pinned separately under case_kind 'parse_fail'.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject

input_blob_hex.description: A structurally malformed blob (hex), empty allowed. The decoder rejects it BEFORE attempting any decryption — magic / protocol_version / format / length checks all run before the AEAD stage (§9.23.1 magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline).

expected_error.description: The specific structural reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: ChatsCatalogError::{MagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, FormatUnsupported, HeaderTooShort, CiphertextTruncated, CiphertextLenOverflow}). Unlike the AEAD failure surface (case_kind decrypt_aead_fail), these are pre-decryption and intentionally distinguishable.
